title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Token Grammar. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (No image generator on this machine, so the build runs code-led whichever you choose.)

options.label: Token Grammar
options.lineage: the code editor's syntax-highlight grammar, promoted to a whole editorial design system
options.thesis: Khalil colors interfaces for a living — so the portfolio itself is typed like code. Every element carries a lexer's role: labels as comments, titles as definitions, quotes as strings, actions as keywords. The color system stops decorating and starts meaning.
options.viewport: A working editor surface, not a hero: the newest shipped interface fragment is the open document, the statement about Khalil set around it as tokenized text — comment labels, keyword actions — cursor blinking at the work, not the name.
options.risk: One hairline from a fake terminal: if tokens decorate instead of typing real content, the grammar collapses into gimmick.

raised.raise: Timed to the margin — every index entry carries tabular metadata (year, stack, role) right-ruled like a tracklist's running times.
Frame-accurate artifacts — every motion or visual artifact is bound to the exact element that earned it; no generic filters.
One continuous section — the page reads as a single ruled strip with tabular time stamps and annotations pinned to structure.
Palette law — the keyword accent is reserved with legal restraint; decorative layers are togglable capability layers, off under reduced motion.

options.label: The Diff
options.thesis: Every project ships as a diff: additions and deletions, before and after, impact written in the exact notation this audience reads all day.
options.viewport: One big honest diff as the first viewport: the before state on one side, Khalil's shipped after on the other, the +lines telling the story of what changed.
options.risk: Diff motifs are a known dev-portfolio device — effective, and also the direction many runs in this category land on.

options.label: Bass Title Sequence
options.thesis: The portfolio as a timed title sequence: flat saturated fields, cut-paper symbols, one idea per card, and scroll scrubs the reel.
options.viewport: A full-bleed burnt-orange card: a black paper shape building the product's name, credits ranked as timed cards, one idea per screen.
options.case: Holds identification — unforgettable and profoundly anti-template. Loses clarity: one-idea-per-card fights dense bilingual case-study content.
options.risk: Sequence pacing burdens a content-heavy portfolio; bilingual type must be cut twice.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: One central event — the practice — radiating tracks: projects, writing, and demos curving out through detector layers; pick a track and the rest dim.
options.viewport: The frozen collision: the hero event held still, tracks labeled by discipline, confidence written as line weight, one track already isolated.
options.case: Holds identification — distinctive and technically credible. Loses clarity: editorial content needs metaphor scaffolding where token grammar maps with zero translation loss.
options.risk: Metaphor load on real content; WebGL weight on a bilingual site.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.case: Fuses poorly: founders and agencies do not live in cassette ephemera.
options.kept: Running-time metadata ruled tight to the margin.

options.label: 16mm Bloom
options.case: Wear and scratch aesthetics contradict the polished-craft product truth.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.case: The architects' world, not this audience's daily reading.
options.kept: The one-continuous-section page with tabular time stamps.

options.label: CRT Arcade
options.case: Phosphor-near-black is exactly the AI-portfolio rut; a strict tile grid fights editorial density.
options.kept: Palette law and togglable capability layers.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The portfolio every web developer ships: hero with name and role, service cards, work grid, testimonial, contact — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name, role, two CTAs, featured project just below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
